patch.value: Use SDK settings-aware item reads and guarded sync persistence

Adopt both unused SDK capabilities from the 2026-10-25 audit: settings-aware locateItem and commitItemMutations match preconditions. Preserve raw-document hashes and ordinary sync output; prove configured lookup and concurrent-write refusal with real non-git trackers, origin/main differential evidence and behavioural revert tests.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Orientation found no existing SDK-adoption item. Related SDK certification: pm-ado-qq1p; source features: pm-ado-4x3u and pm-ado-nc7z. Both audited SDK APIs exist in the pinned 2026.10.23 dependency. Plan: preserve authoritative raw documents, replace unguarded sync persistence with inspected-snapshot match preconditions, run non-git regression/differential/revert proofs and unchanged npm/Bun release gates.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Both replacements implemented. Resolution passes readSettings item_format and resolveItemTypeRegistry type_to_folder into locateItem and retains readLocatedItem whole-document hashing. Sync now uses commitItemMutations update match on inspected updated_at for link, relation and base writes. Expected revisions advance from our own immutable SDK transaction history, never from a refreshed current item. Three new real non-git regressions pass: custom nested folder/raw-document guard, local edit after Azure PATCH, and local edit before import relation/base persistence. The last two preserve the concurrent item/history bytes and return ADO_CONFLICT; remote success can remain partial.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Compatibility check found SDK gap tracked by pm-ado-sdk-match-close-1025: match on updated_at also runs inside update's internal terminal close after its first write has advanced the timestamp. Workaround uses one SDK transaction with a guarded scalar update then explicit close. SDK history messages necessarily become bulk-item-transaction markers instead of adapter prose; this intentional diagnostic difference is documented and differential-tested. Initial read-only differential passed over public pm-ado and pm-jira origin snapshots: 140 items, 8 exact output comparisons, unchanged authoritative bytes. Extending proof to writable copies for persistence receipts, values and history patches.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Revert proof, lookup: restored only AdoResolutionService.document from origin/main, rebuilt dist, then node --test --test-name-pattern='SDK lookup' test/sync.test.ts failed 1/1 as expected (custom nested folder scope refusal). Revert proof, sync: replaced only the local update helper with ordinary pm.update, rebuilt dist, then node --test --test-name-pattern='SDK sync match' test/sync.test.ts failed 2/2 as expected (newer local edits overwritten / success instead of conflict). Restored both implementations and rebuilt: all 4 targeted tests pass, including terminal lifecycle compatibility. No history records were rewritten.

value.text: Differential PASS: origin/main 7f44a1d build versus candidate, public pm-ado 7f44a1d (32 items) and pm-jira 2fd1537 (108 items). Total 14 comparisons over 140 real items. Only intentional difference in ordinary writes is mandatory SDK transaction history messages; both old/new forms asserted. Full method and reproducible command in docs/sdk-adoption.md.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Blocking cases now pass on real non-git trackers. Closing is a scalar update then a status-only update, each commitItemMutations update carrying the revision from our previous immutable history event; no unguarded close remains. Durable scoped outbox intents precede Azure create/PATCH, with creation keys derived from local id + operation + original plan and stamped in reserved Azure tags. Retry resolves the marker before creation and preserves local edits when completing a failed link. PATCH carries a revision assertion and history marker. A recording REST/interleaving/real SIGKILL matrix is running. Provider limitation: ambiguous create dispatch with no visible marker must fail closed to avoid a second POST; automatic convergence in that ambiguous case requires a server uniqueness guarantee not present in the documented Work Item Create API. Clarification requested while remaining work continues.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Provider constraint remains unresolved: the documented Azure Work Item Create API has no server-enforced idempotency key or unique-tag precondition. A crash between durable dispatch and actual POST cannot guarantee both zero duplicates and automatic convergence. Implementation preserves the intent, retries exact marker lookup, and refuses another POST while the outcome is unknown. The orchestrator was asked whether fail-closed recovery is acceptable or a uniqueness service exists; no approval has been assumed. Crash tests explicitly distinguish this held state from convergence after provider visibility. No live Azure call was made.
